# AF 第四章 原文（重制基线）

## Chapter 4

[P01] By late summer, news of Animal Farm had spread across half the county（县）. Every day Snowball and Napoleon sent out pigeons to mix with animals on nearby farms, tell them about the uprising（起义）, and teach them the tune of 'Animals of England'. Mr. Jones sat in the Red Lion at Willingdon. He complained about the injustice（不公） done to him. A pack of useless（无用） animals had turned him out of his own property（财产）. The other farmers felt sorry for him, but at first gave him little help.

[P02] In their hearts, each wondered if he could turn Jones's bad luck into something good for himself. Luckily, the owners of the two farms next to Animal Farm were always on bad terms. One was called Foxwood（狐林）. It was a large, old farm that nobody cared for. Trees had grown over much of it, all its fields were worn out, and its hedges（树篱） were in a shameful（可耻） state. Its owner, Mr. Pilkington, was a relaxed gentleman farmer who spent most of his time fishing or hunting. The other farm, Pinchfield（窄地）, was smaller and better kept. Its owner, Mr. Frederick, was a tough（艰难）, clever man who was always in lawsuits（诉讼） and was known for driving hard bargains（交易）.

[P03] These two disliked（讨厌） each other so much that they could hardly agree on anything, even to protect their own interests. Still, both were very afraid of the uprising on Animal Farm. They did not want their own animals to learn too much about it. At first they pretended to laugh at the idea of animals running a farm. The whole thing would be over in two weeks, they said. They spread the news that the animals on the farm (they would not accept the name "Animal Farm") were always fighting and were quickly starving（挨饿） to death.

[P04] As time went on, the animals did not starve（饿死）. So Frederick and Pilkington changed their tune. They began to talk about the wickedness（邪恶） on Animal Farm. People were told the animals ate their own kind, tortured（折磨） one another, and shared their females. Frederick and Pilkington said this came from rebelling（反叛） against Nature's laws. However, these stories were not fully believed. Rumours（谣言） of a wonderful farm, where human beings were turned out and animals ran their own affairs（事务）, went on spreading in vague（模糊） and twisted（扭曲） forms. All that year a wave of rebelliousness（叛逆） ran through the countryside.

[P05] Bulls（公牛） that had always been easy to control suddenly became wild. Sheep broke down hedges and ate the clover. Cows kicked the pail（桶） over. Hunters（猎人） refused their fences and threw their riders（骑手） on to the other side. Above all, the tune and even the words of 'animals of England' were known everywhere. People could not hold their anger when they heard this song, though they pretended to think it only funny. They said they could not understand how animals could sing such worthless（无用） rubbish. Any animal caught singing it was whipped on the spot（地点）. And yet the song could not be stopped.

[P06] The blackbirds（黑鸟） whistled（吹哨） it in the hedges, the pigeons cooed（咕咕叫） it in the elms（榆树）. It got into the noise of the smithies（铁匠铺） and the sound of the church bells. When people heard it, they shook with fear inside. They felt it told of their bad future. Early in October, the corn was cut and stacked（堆叠）, and some was already threshed（打谷）. A flight of pigeons came whirling（旋转） through the air and landed in the yard of Animal Farm in great excitement.

[P07] Jones and all his men, with half a dozen others from Foxwood（狐林） and Pinchfield（窄地）, came through the five-barred（阻挡） gate and moved up the cart-track to the farm. They all had sticks, but Jones walked in front with a gun. Clearly they wanted to take the farm back. The animals had expected this and were ready. Snowball had read an old book about Julius（朱利叶斯） Caesar（凯撒）'s campaigns（战役）. He was in charge（冲锋） of the defence（防御）. He gave orders fast, and in a couple of minutes every animal was at his post. As the men came near the farm buildings, Snowball began his first attack.

[P08] All thirty-five pigeons flew over the men's heads and dropped on them. While the men were busy, the geese, hiding behind the hedge（树篱）, rushed out and pecked（啄） hard at their legs. However, this was only a light fight, and the men easily drove the geese off with sticks. Snowball then started his second attack. Muriel, Benjamin, all the sheep, and Snowball at the head rushed forward and butted the men from every side, while Benjamin turned and hit them with his small hoofs.

[P09] But the men, with their sticks and heavy boots, were too strong for them again. Then Snowball gave a squeal（尖叫）—the signal（信号） to retreat（撤退）—and all the animals turned and ran through the gateway（入口） into the yard. The men shouted in triumph（胜利）. They thought their enemies were running away, so they rushed after them in disorder（混乱）. This was just what Snowball wanted. Once the men were well inside the yard, the three horses, the three cows, and the other pigs, who had been hiding in the cowshed（牛棚）, suddenly came out behind them and cut them off.

[P10] Snowball gave the signal to charge. He ran straight at Jones. Jones raised his gun and fired. The pellets（颗粒） cut bloody（血腥） lines along Snowball's back, and a sheep fell dead. Without stopping, Snowball threw his fifteen stone against Jones's legs. Jones fell into a pile of dung（粪便） and his gun flew out of his hands. But the most terrifying（可怕） sight was Boxer, standing on his back legs and hitting out with his great iron-shod（装蹄） hoofs. His first blow hit a stable-lad（马童） from Foxwood on the head and stretched（伸展） him lifeless（无生命） in the mud.

[P11] At the sight, several men dropped their sticks and tried to run. Panic took them, and the next moment all the animals were chasing（追赶） them round the yard. They were gored（刺伤）, kicked, bitten, and stepped on. Every animal took revenge（复仇） in his own way. Even the cat jumped off a roof onto a cowman（牛夫）'s shoulders and sank her claws（爪子） in his neck, and he yelled（喊叫） horribly（可怕地）. When the way was clear, the men rushed out and ran for the main road.

[P12] And so, within five minutes of their invasion（入侵）, they were running away in shame, going back by the same way they had come. A flock（羊群） of geese hissed after them and pecked at their legs all the way. Every man was gone except one. Back in the yard, Boxer was pawing（刨地） with his hoof（蹄） at the stable-lad（马童） who lay face down in the mud, trying to turn him over.

[P13] The boy did not move. "He is dead," said Boxer sadly. "I did not mean to do that. I forgot I was wearing iron shoes. Who will believe I did not do this on purpose?" "No sentimentality（感伤）, comrade（同志）!" cried Snowball. "War is war. The only good human being is a dead one." "I do not want to take life, not even human life," "Where is Mollie?" Boxer said, his eyes full of tears."Where is Mollie?" cried somebody. Mollie was missing. Everyone was very afraid; they feared the men might have hurt her, or taken her away.

[P14] In the end, they found her hiding in her stall（畜栏）, head buried in the hay（干草） in the manger（食槽）. She had run away when the gun went off. The stable-lad（马童）, only stunned（震惊）, had got better and run off. The animals came together in wild excitement, each telling his brave deeds（事迹） in the battle loudly. A celebration（庆祝） was held at once. The flag was run up and 'animals of England' was sung many times, then the dead sheep was given a solemn（庄严） funeral, a hawthorn（山楂） bush planted on her grave（坟墓）.

[P15] At the grave, Snowball made a short speech. He said all animals must be ready to die for Animal Farm if they had to. The animals all agreed to make a military（军事） honour, "Animal Hero, First Class." It was given right there to Snowball and Boxer. It was a brass（黄铜） medal (really some old horse-brasses（铜牌） found in the harness（马具）-room), to be worn on Sundays and holidays. There was also "Animal Hero, Second Class," given to the dead sheep after her death. They talked a lot about what to call the battle.

[P16] In the end, they named it the Battle of the Cowshed, because the ambush（埋伏） started there. They found Jones's gun in the mud, and knew there were cartridges（弹药） in the farmhouse（农舍）. They decided to put the gun at the foot of the Flagstaff（旗杆）, like a piece of artillery（大炮）, and to fire it twice a year--once on October the twelfth, the anniversary（周年） of the Battle of the Cowshed, and once on Midsummer（仲夏） Day, the anniversary of the uprising.
